inputs.base_year_fcf_note: FY2026E FCF (estimated at ~14% FCF margin on $83.5B guided revenue midpoint), used as Year 0 starting point for projections
inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026E revenue midpoint of company guidance ($82-85B); Year 0 base for revenue projections

historical_growth.fcf_cagr_note: FCF CAGRs are compressed by anomalously low FY2023 ($792.5M due to heavy capex + Lilly ICOS acquisition) and elevated capex in FY2024 ($3,760M). FY2025 FCF of $8,972M represents normalized recovery. FCF margin is rising (13.8% in FY2025, ~15.2% in Q1 2026).
historical_growth.equity_cagr_note: Equity growth driven by retained earnings (net income); shares outstanding declined slightly from 912.5M (FY2020) to 899.3M (FY2025) — no material dilution. FY2025 equity jump ($14.3B -> $26.5B) reflects $20.6B net income minus dividends/buybacks.
historical_growth.growth_rate_rationale: For a high-growth large-cap pharma with a dominant GLP-1 franchise, revenue CAGR is the most defensible primary driver. Equity CAGR (35.4%) overstates sustainable growth since it is mechanically driven by explosive net income in FY2024-FY2025 accumulating on a low base. FCF CAGR is distorted downward by elevated capex cycle. Revenue 5yr CAGR of 21.6% aligns with company guidance deceleration trajectory and independent analyst estimates. Base case growth rates are set to decelerate from near-term guidance levels (~28% in FY2026) toward mid-single digits by year 5.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: REVIEW: Equity 3yr CAGR (35.0%) vs Revenue 3yr CAGR (31.7%) diverges by 3.4pp — within 30pp threshold, no flag. Equity 5yr CAGR (35.4%) vs Revenue 5yr CAGR (21.6%) diverges by 13.8pp — within 30pp threshold. EPS 3yr CAGR (49.3%) materially exceeds revenue 3yr (31.7%) by 17.6pp — reflects operating leverage kicking in as GLP-1 franchise scaled. Primary driver switched to revenue_5yr_cagr as most conservative and transparent metric for this business.

base.narrative: Sustained near-term hypergrowth driven by Mounjaro/Zepbound volume expansion (guided 40%+ volume in 2026), partially offset by ~low-to-mid teens price headwind. Growth decelerates meaningfully in years 3-5 as the revenue base scales, competition intensifies, and legacy product erosion (Trulicity biosimilar 2027) becomes material. FCF margins expand from ~14% (FY2026E) toward 22% in Year 5 as manufacturing capex cycle moderates and operating leverage matures.

bull.narrative: GLP-1 penetration accelerates beyond current trajectory; Foundayo (orforglipron) captures a new patient cohort, adding $8-10B by Year 3; retatrutide achieves Phase 3 success and NDA approval by 2027, layering additional blockbuster revenue. International markets (Europe, Japan, China) contribute meaningfully. M&A diversification reduces tirzepatide concentration risk, sustaining premium multiple. FCF margins benefit from oral small-molecule economics (lower COGS vs. injectable) and manufacturing leverage.

bear.narrative: Realized price erosion widens beyond guided low-to-mid teens to 20%+ as MFN/TrumpRx expands, LillyDirect self-pay volumes grow at lower ASPs, and PBM rebate pressure intensifies. Novo Nordisk oral semaglutide captures outsized share of oral GLP-1 market, capping Foundayo's uptake. Retatrutide misses primary endpoint or faces label restriction. Trulicity biosimilar entry in 2027 accelerates legacy revenue decline. Higher WACC reflects increased execution risk and multiple compression from premium to sector-average.

sensitivity.note: Matrix shows Base Case intrinsic value per share at each WACC / terminal growth rate combination. Base case growth rates and FCF margins held constant; only discount rate and terminal growth vary. WACC rows top-to-bottom: 7.5%, 8.0%, 8.5%, 9.0%, 9.5%. Terminal growth columns left-to-right: 2.0%, 2.5%, 3.0%, 3.5%, 4.0%.

probability_weighted.note: Weighted IV = (0.25 x $1,188.60) + (0.50 x $647.24) + (0.25 x $296.09) = $694.79. At $1,107 current price, LLY trades at a ~60% premium to base-case intrinsic value and at 59% above probability-weighted IV. Bull case IV ($1,189) barely exceeds current price (+7.4%), suggesting the stock is pricing in a scenario requiring near-flawless execution on GLP-1 growth, pipeline success, and FCF conversion.

key_assumptions_summary.primary_growth_driver: revenue_5yr_cagr (21.58%); applied with business-cycle deceleration from 28% in Year 1 to 9% in Year 5
key_assumptions_summary.fcf_projection_method: Revenue growth applied to FY2026E base ($83.5B); FCF projected as margin % of revenue improving from 16% to 22% as operating leverage scales and capex cycle moderates
key_assumptions_summary.wacc_rationale: Base WACC 8.5%: risk-free rate ~4.3%, equity risk premium ~5.0%, beta ~0.85 for large-cap pharma with non-cyclical demand. Adjusted slightly upward vs. pure CAPM for tirzepatide concentration risk. Net debt ~$38B is manageable against $65B+ revenue base.
key_assumptions_summary.terminal_growth_rationale: 3.0% base: consistent with nominal long-term GDP growth. GLP-1 franchise has genuine durable demand (obesity/diabetes are chronic), but patent cliff for tirzepatide in early 2030s creates structural uncertainty warranting a measured terminal assumption rather than 4%+.
key_risks_to_valuation: Price erosion beyond guided low-to-mid teens could compress FCF margins materially
Tirzepatide patent challenge or unexpected safety event
Novo Nordisk oral semaglutide capturing disproportionate oral GLP-1 market share
Retatrutide Phase 3 failure removing the next growth wave
Valuation multiple compression if growth disappoints

historical_averages.note: FY2020-FY2025 calendar FY-end Dec closing prices. EV/EBITDA uses EBITDA estimated as OperatingIncome x 1.12 (D&A approx).

sanity_check.diagnosis: No trip. Base-case intrinsic value $647.24 implies P/E ~28x, P/B ~22x, EV/EBITDA ~21x on FY2025 actuals — all BELOW LLY's 6-year historical averages (P/E 56x, P/B 36x, EV/EBITDA 44x). The DCF is conservative relative to the multiples the market has consistently paid; it concludes LLY is OVERvalued at $1,107 (base upside -41.5%), the opposite of the SEK.NZ over-valuation failure mode the sanity check guards against. The high-multiple history reflects the market pricing in extraordinary GLP-1 franchise growth that a decelerating DCF deliberately does not fully extrapolate.
